title: Holidays
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 7). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

stops.title: N-400 card: Willing to bear arms

facts: Independence Day, on July 4, celebrates U.S. independence from Britain. It is the country's birthday.
Memorial Day, in May, honors soldiers who died in military service.

newWords.meaning: to do something special for a happy day
July 4, the day the Declaration of Independence was adopted

help.simpler: Independence Day is a holiday on the fourth of July.
help.example: Many people call it “the Fourth of July.”
help.why: The test asks what Independence Day is.

story.say: It celebrates U.S. independence from Britain.

help.simpler: On this day, Americans remember becoming free from Britain.
help.example: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.

help.simpler: July 4 is when the country celebrates its birthday.
help.example: Many people watch fireworks and have picnics.
help.why: “The country’s birthday” is an answer on the test.

help.simpler: Memorial Day is a holiday at the end of May.
help.example: It is always on a Monday.

story.say: It honors soldiers who died in military service.

help.simpler: On Memorial Day, Americans remember soldiers who died.
help.example: To honor means to show respect.

facts: Veterans Day, in November, honors people who have served in the U.S. military.

National holidays include New Year's Day, Martin Luther King, Jr. Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day.
For the test, you can name any three of them.

newWords.meaning: a person who served in the military
a day the whole country celebrates
a national holiday on the fourth Thursday of November where people eat turkey and lots of food.
